title: 95% of the universe is fine print
logline: Gus says he has read the whole universe. Vera shows him the 95% he skipped.
description: Atoms are only about 5% of the universe; the rest is dark matter and dark energy. Sources and simplifications in the pinned comment. What else would you put in the fine print?

claims.text: Today's mass-energy budget of the universe is about 5% ordinary matter, 27% dark matter and 68% dark energy.
claims.source: Planck Collaboration, Planck 2018 results VI: Cosmological parameters, A&A 641, A6 (2020); NASA Science, 'Dark Energy, Dark Matter'

claims.text: Stars in the outer parts of galaxies orbit faster than the visible mass can explain (flat rotation curves), a key line of evidence for dark matter.
claims.source: Rubin & Ford 1970; Rubin, Ford & Thonnard 1980; OpenStax, Astronomy 2e, dark matter section (check section number)

claims.text: Distant Type Ia supernovae are dimmer than expected, showing that the expansion of the universe is accelerating.
claims.source: Riess et al. 1998; Perlmutter et al. 1999; The Nobel Prize in Physics 2011 (nobelprize.org)

claims.text: Dark energy is the name for whatever drives the acceleration; neither dark energy nor dark matter has been identified.

simplifications: The shares are of the universe's total mass-energy today, not of its volume. They change over cosmic time.
'Atoms' means ordinary (baryonic) matter: it also counts the gas between galaxies, which we mostly don't see. Neutrinos and light are a tiny extra slice, left out.
Rotation curves are one line of evidence for dark matter; gravitational lensing and the cosmic microwave background are others.
The numbers are rounded; 4.9 + 26.8 + 68.3 is the usual Planck split.

figures.label: What the universe is made of (%)

lines.text: Done. I've read the whole universe: stars, planets, gas.
All the atoms? About 5% of it.
lines.spoken: All the atoms? About five percent of it.

lines.text: So the other 95% is… more planets?
lines.spoken: So the other ninety-five percent is… more planets?

lines.text: 27% is dark matter. Galaxies spin too fast without it.
lines.spoken: Twenty-seven percent is dark matter. Galaxies spin too fast without it.

lines.text: 68% is dark energy. Far-off supernovae show the expansion speeding up.
lines.spoken: Sixty-eight percent is dark energy. Far-off supernovae show the expansion speeding up.

lines.text: Everything you've ever touched is in that 5%.
lines.spoken: Everything you've ever touched is in that five percent.

lines.text: You read the 5%. The rest is fine print.
lines.spoken: You read the five percent. The rest is fine print.
